stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid co-orbital worries
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C at a $1.6 billion valuation, highlighting the increasing interest in co-orbital security solutions. This funding comes as concerns about Russia's co-orbital activities near commercial GEO slots raise eyebrows among insurers and operators alike. The DoD's push for space domain awareness is clearly paying off.
stories.soWhat: In an era where orbital security is paramount, True Anomaly's funding isn't just cash—it's a signal that investors are betting on the future of space defense.

stories.head: Rocket Lab proves small rockets can party too
stories.body: Rocket Lab successfully launched its 10th Synspective satellite, reinforcing the idea that small rockets can maintain a busy launch schedule. This mission adds to Rocket Lab's growing portfolio, proving that even the little guys can make a big impact in the satellite market. With increasing demand for small satellite launches, Rocket Lab is clearly in the right lane.
stories.soWhat: Rocket Lab's success suggests that the small satellite launch market is maturing, leaving larger players to rethink their strategies in a crowded space.

stories.head: Spain backs FOSSA with $10.5M for satellite push
stories.body: FOSSA Systems raised $10.5 million with backing from a Spanish fund, aiming to enhance sovereign satellite communications. This funding reflects a growing trend among European nations to bolster their space capabilities, especially in the face of increasing geopolitical tensions. It's clear that even satellites need a financial safety net these days.
stories.soWhat: The Spanish investment in FOSSA signals a shift towards more localized satellite capabilities, potentially reshaping the European space landscape in the coming years.

watchlist.title: Watch for satellite communications trends

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
